reconcile.connective: The standard defense is chronological: Abraham's marriage predated the Levitical code, and marrying a paternal half-sister was reckoned lawful in that era.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses the tension directly: God blesses Abraham's marriage to his paternal half-sister in Genesis, yet Leviticus and Deuteronomy curse that very union as incest.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Is incest forbidden?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/incest.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013), "Is incest forbidden?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: and she became my wife; as in those times it was judged lawful, and so it has been accounted lawful in many nations to marry sisters on the father's side, when those on the mother's were prohibited …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly harmonizes by appeal to era: Abraham's marriage to a paternal half-sister was lawful at that time, before the later Levitical prohibition — the core chronological defense, keyed to the exact verse and relationship in tension.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Genesis 20:12
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact verse, explaining Sarah as Abraham's paternal half-sister and arguing such father-side marriages were judged lawful in that era, before the Levitical code.

link.title: Defending Inerrancy: Is there a Bible contradiction in Genesis 20:12?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment of the Abraham/Sarah half-sister marriage vs. the Levitical incest laws; argues the chronological gap plus the breadth of the term 'sister'.
